hooks.title: Wagons Turned Back
hooks.text: Grand Syndic Geadeth has closed the border to carts from Sweyemlel, and the carters' guild is threatening to march on Sweyemoth. Hierarch Gliril needs proof the blockade breaks an old treaty.

hooks.title: The Closed Border
hooks.text: By order of Hierarch Gliril, no wagon may cross into Transe. The merchants of Sweyemoth are quietly paying anyone who can get their goods through regardless.

hooks.title: The Tax Strike
hooks.text: Hierarch Gliril takes 14 in every hundred on trade, about 25148 sp a year, and the towns grumble. A pamphleteer calling for a tax strike must be found, or protected, depending on who pays.

hooks.title: Opened Graves
hooks.text: Old graves from the Weeping Fever have been opened in the night. The folk of Sweyemlel whisper that someone wants the sickness back.

hooks.title: Treasure-Hunters
hooks.text: Treasure-hunters are digging at Laeliemere, near Sweyemoth. Hierarch Gliril wants them stopped, or wants a share.

reasons: About 10,132 sp of goods pass between them each year.
They have fought two wars in recorded memory.
Two settlements changed hands between them by the sword.
The last war between them ended only 23 years ago.
About 11,451 sp of goods pass between them each year.
They have fought four wars in recorded memory.
Two settlements changed hands between them by the sword.

events.title: The founding of Sweyemlel
events.text: Wearied of paying tribute to everyone, 0 settlements around Sweyemoth agree to answer to one table, and call it Sweyemlel.

events.title: Sweyemlel begins under House Labrook
events.text: The oath-fires of Sweyemlel are lit for House Labrook of Sweyemoth, first of its rulers.

events.title: Hierarch Randas of Sweyemlel
events.text: With the old ruler's seal on a ribbon around the neck, Randas of House Labrook becomes Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: House Rieleaf elected in Sweyemlel
events.text: The ring of the elders is passed to House Rieleaf, and Sweyemlel has a new ruling family.
events.name: The Moot of Rieleaf
events.backstory: The custom of Sweyemlel is to choose its rulers, and in 50 the electors passed over Labrook for House Rieleaf.

events.title: Hierarch Fision of Sweyemlel
events.text: Fision of House Rieleaf is raised as Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The Dylemlefeth War
events.text: Old grievances at Dylemlefeth set Sweyemlel and Transe at each other's throats.
events.name: The Dylemlefeth War
events.backstory: Sweyemlel raised the toll on Dylemlefeth bridge, Transe refused to pay, and the Dylemlefeth War was the result.

events.title: The Treaty of Dylemlefeth
events.text: After years of burnt barns and empty cradles, Sweyemlel and Transe agree that nothing was worth it, and change no boundary.

events.title: House Vianawood elected in Sweyemlel
events.text: Delegates gather at Sweyemoth and, after three days of argument, choose House Vianawood to rule Sweyemlel.
events.name: The Raising of House Vianawood
events.backstory: The custom of Sweyemlel is to choose its rulers, and in 76 the electors passed over Rieleaf for House Vianawood.

events.title: Hierarch Thielas of Sweyemlel
events.text: Thielas takes the seat of Sweyemlel.

events.title: High water at Edede
events.text: The river lifts over its banks, and Edede stand in brown water.
events.backstory: A bank of the Meglibrook gave way in 76 above Edede, and the water had nowhere else to go.

events.title: Silt over Miglade
events.text: The flood leaves Miglade under silt; nobody rebuilds the farmstead.
events.backstory: Miglade lay in the path of the flood of 76, and the farmstead was given up in 77.

events.title: Hierarch Siathiel of Sweyemlel
events.text: With the old ruler's seal on a ribbon around the neck, Siathiel of House Vianawood becomes Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The fall of the Uklu galleries
events.text: Old galleries give way beneath Uklu, burying a shift of miners.
events.backstory: The mine owners at Uklu skimped on props, and the miners paid for it in 103.

events.title: High water at Uklu
events.text: The river lifts over its banks, and Uklu stand in brown water.
events.name: The Great Meglibrook Spate
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Uklu in 106.

events.title: Ninmoch in flames
events.text: A fire in the lower lanes burns a third of Ninmoch.
events.name: The Burning Night of Ninmoch
events.backstory: The blaze began with a forgotten lamp in a chandler's loft; by morning Ninmoch was ash.

events.title: The burning of Haholm
events.text: A lamp left burning ends Haholm; the survivors will not build again on the ashes of the charcoal-burners' camp.
events.backstory: The Burning Night of Ninmoch took Haholm; the charcoal-burners' camp was not rebuilt after 108.

events.title: The Sedcheshch Quarrel
events.text: Raiding and reprisals around Sedcheshch turn into open war between Sweyemlel and Transe.
events.name: The Sedcheshch Quarrel
events.backstory: Merchants complained of bribes and double charges at Sedcheshch until Sweyemlel and Transe chose swords over ledgers.

events.title: The Peace of Sedcheshch
events.text: Sweyemlel has the better of it, and Transe gives up Sedcheshch.

events.title: Sedcheshch passes to Sweyemlel
events.text: The folk of Sedcheshch wake to find themselves subjects of Sweyemlel.
events.backstory: Sedcheshch was one of the spoils of the Sedcheshch Quarrel, and changed hands in 124 without a single arrow.

events.title: The Blue Rot
events.text: First seen at Nere, the sickness follows carters and pilgrims to Ichgal, Wichchyl, Schilchynch and 31 other places.
events.name: The Blue Rot
events.backstory: No single cause was ever named for the Blue Rot, though the poorest quarter of Nere suffered first.

events.title: Sheep replace the folk of Laeliemere
events.text: A new boundary ditch cuts Laeliemere off from its common, and the charcoal-burners' camp fades into the pasture.

events.title: Hierarch Thysylith the Hard of Sweyemlel
events.text: Thysylith the Hard of House Vianawood is raised as Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The War of the Sweyemlel Marches
events.text: Envoys from Ykar and Sweyemlel part in anger at Ethefkolf, and within the season both are mustering.
events.name: The War of the Sweyemlel Marches
events.backstory: It began as an argument over tolls at Ethefkolf, and by 144 both Ykar and Sweyemlel had armies in the field.

events.title: High water at Rorern
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Edede and Rorern.
events.backstory: The Meglibrook rose a fathom in a night in 144, and Rorern had no time to carry its goods up the hill.

events.title: The Peace of Ethefkolf
events.text: After years of burnt barns and empty cradles, Ykar and Sweyemlel agree that nothing was worth it, and change no boundary.

events.title: The Ember Rash comes to Transe
events.text: Carried along the roads from Chraagagaut, it empties houses in Snichrogse, Erchatral, Chlichoch and 34 other places.
events.name: The Ember Rash
events.backstory: When the Ember Rash reached Chraagagaut, the people were still lean from the Black Granary Winters, and it killed them in droves.

events.title: Hierarch Liera of Sweyemlel
events.text: With the old ruler's seal on a ribbon around the neck, Liera of House Vianawood becomes Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: High water at Bornen
events.text: Water runs through the streets of Sedcheshch and Bornen and down into the cellars.
events.name: The Flood of the Broken Banks of 168
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Bornen in 168.

events.title: The fall of the Schilonich galleries
events.text: The deep workings at Schilonich come down on the night shift.
events.backstory: Water pooled in the old workings at Schilonich for a season, and in 168 it burst through into the working face.

events.title: Skysund dies of thirst
events.text: The well at Skysund fails in a dry summer, and the mill hamlet is left to the crows.

events.title: Veglen is abandoned
events.text: Water must be hauled from far off to Veglen; in the end the hunters' lodge is simply abandoned.

events.title: The great flood at Eeyede
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Eeyede.
events.name: The Drowning of Eeyede
events.backstory: Heavy rain upstream pushed the Meglibrook over its banks in 190, and Eeyede was caught asleep.

events.title: Viabrook lost to the water
events.text: The river takes the well, the fields and the footbridge of Viabrook, and the charcoal-burners' camp is let go.
events.backstory: After the Drowning of Eeyede the people of Viabrook rebuilt nothing; the charcoal-burners' camp was empty by 190.

events.title: The Chagshot War
events.text: Old grievances at Chagshot set Sweyemlel and Transe at each other's throats.
events.name: The Chagshot War
events.backstory: It began as an argument over tolls at Chagshot, and by 193 both Sweyemlel and Transe had armies in the field.

events.title: Sewood dies of thirst
events.text: Water must be hauled from far off to Sewood; in the end the charcoal-burners' camp is simply abandoned.

events.title: The electors of Sweyemlel choose
events.text: With no clear heir, the notables of Sweyemlel vote, and House Miathorn wins by a handful of voices.
events.name: The Moot of Miathorn
events.backstory: The custom of Sweyemlel is to choose its rulers, and in 197 the electors passed over Vianawood for House Miathorn.

events.title: Hierarch Glethion of Sweyemlel
events.text: Glethion takes the seat of Sweyemlel.

events.title: Naesund is abandoned
events.text: Naesund is attacked in the dark twice in a year, and the shepherds' steading is then left to the owls.

events.title: Raiders at Fedell
events.text: Raiders return to Fedell each autumn until the mill hamlet has nothing worth the trouble.

events.title: The Peace of Chagshot
events.text: Neither side can claim victory; Sweyemlel and Transe swap hostages and go home.

events.title: A new house at Sweyemoth
events.text: The last heir of the old line is buried, and House Faleaf is named to follow them.
events.name: The Crown Without Heir
events.backstory: Miathorn left no children, and the councillors of Sweyemlel gave the crown to House Faleaf to avoid a war.

events.title: Hierarch Glianith the Lawgiver of Sweyemlel
events.text: Glianith the Lawgiver of House Faleaf is raised as Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: High water at Chogtol
events.text: The river bursts its banks and drowns the low fields of Chogtol.
events.backstory: Heavy rain upstream pushed the Meglibrook over its banks in 212, and Chogtol was caught asleep.

events.title: The Welefeth flood
events.text: Water runs through the streets of Welefeth and down into the cellars.
events.backstory: A warm wind in 214 melted the winter snow in a week, and the Meglibrook filled faster than any dyke could be raised.

events.title: Raiders at Fyglen
events.text: Raiders return to Fyglen each autumn until the mill hamlet has nothing worth the trouble.

events.title: Elaeliawood is abandoned
events.text: Sheep are worth more to the lord than tenants, and the hamlet at Elaeliawood is cleared.

events.title: The War for Chagshot
events.text: Sweyemlel and Transe go to war over the country around Chagshot.
events.name: The War for Chagshot
events.backstory: Merchants complained of bribes and double charges at Chagshot until Sweyemlel and Transe chose swords over ledgers.

events.title: Sweyemlel under a conqueror's house
events.text: The victors of the war set House Sybrook on the throne of Sweyemlel, and the old rulers are not seen again.
events.name: The Humbling of Sweyemlel
events.backstory: The War for Chagshot ended with Faleaf defeated, and the victors put House Sybrook on the throne of Sweyemlel.

events.title: Hierarch Mialion of Sweyemlel
events.text: Mialion of House Sybrook is raised as Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The Treaty of Chagshot
events.text: Transe has the better of it, and Sweyemlel gives up Chagshot.

events.title: Chagshot passes to Transe
events.text: Chagshot is handed from Sweyemlel to Transe.
events.backstory: After the War for Chagshot, the people of Chagshot found their new lords had little interest in their old customs.

events.title: High water at Schilonich
events.text: The river bursts its banks and drowns the low fields of Schilonich, Chargadrych and Vigrachat.
events.name: The Great Meglibrook Spate of 228
events.backstory: The Meglibrook rose a fathom in a night in 228, and Schilonich had no time to carry its goods up the hill.

events.title: Sheep replace the folk of Nyglade
events.text: The tenants of Nyglade are paid to leave, and the walls of the salt-works village are used for the sheepfold.

events.title: Sheep replace the folk of Alyelibrook
events.text: A new boundary ditch cuts Alyelibrook off from its common, and the hamlet fades into the pasture.

events.title: The Uklu flood
events.text: Water runs through the streets of Uklu and down into the cellars.
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Uklu in 241.

events.title: Hierarch Ryras the Pious of Sweyemlel
events.text: With the old ruler's seal on a ribbon around the neck, Ryras the Pious of House Sybrook becomes Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The dry well of Vymasund
events.text: Water must be hauled from far off to Vymasund; in the end the village is simply abandoned.

events.title: The Weeping Fever at Seflol
events.text: It breaks out in Seflol and spreads to Kakriroy, Ykroy, Rikrym and 160 other places.
events.name: The Weeping Fever
events.backstory: Traders brought the Weeping Fever to Seflol, and it rode their carts as far as Kakriroy, Ykroy, Rikrym and 160 other places.

events.title: Silence at Thyvaglen
events.text: Whole families die at Thyvaglen, and the few who live join kin at Teefethlefeth.
events.backstory: Survivors of the Weeping Fever refused to remain at Thyvaglen, and the charcoal-burners' camp was left to the weeds in 249.

events.title: Silence at Fieliabrook
events.text: The sickness has emptied Fieliabrook; the survivors burn their belongings and walk away from the hamlet.
events.backstory: The sickness of the Weeping Fever reached Fieliabrook; by 250 the hamlet was empty.

events.title: Silence at Faehavn
events.text: No one will touch the doors of Faehavn after the fever, and the ferry village slowly returns to the wild.
events.backstory: The Weeping Fever emptied Faehavn, and the ferry village was abandoned in 251.

events.title: Silence at Elaliglade
events.text: No one will touch the doors of Elaliglade after the fever, and the salt-works village slowly returns to the wild.
events.backstory: Survivors of the Weeping Fever refused to remain at Elaliglade, and the salt-works village was left to the weeds in 251.

events.title: Eliemere dies of thirst
events.text: No one at Eliemere can dig deeper, so the mill hamlet is left to the crows.

events.title: Raiders at Gleglen
events.text: Raiders return to Gleglen each autumn until the farmstead has nothing worth the trouble.

events.title: The great flood at Feelylde
events.text: The river lifts over its banks, and Feelylde stand in brown water.
events.name: The Flood of the Broken Banks of 258
events.backstory: The Meglibrook rose a fathom in a night in 258, and Feelylde had no time to carry its goods up the hill.

events.title: The War of Fethyode
events.text: Ykar and Sweyemlel go to war over the country around Fethyode.
events.name: The War of Fethyode
events.backstory: It began as an argument over tolls at Fethyode, and by 259 both Ykar and Sweyemlel had armies in the field.

events.title: Droholt is abandoned
events.text: Raiders return to Droholt each autumn until the ferry village has nothing worth the trouble.

events.title: The electors of Sweyemlel choose
events.text: The ring of the elders is passed to House Riabrook, and Sweyemlel has a new ruling family.
events.name: The Raising of House Riabrook
events.backstory: Sybrook ruled until 261, when the assembly of Sweyemlel gave the office to House Riabrook.

events.title: Hierarch Alasar of Sweyemlel
events.text: With the old ruler's seal on a ribbon around the neck, Alasar of House Riabrook becomes Hierarch of Sweyemlel.

events.title: The Ekyskolf flood
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Ekyskolf.
events.backstory: Heavy rain upstream pushed the Meglibrook over its banks in 261, and Ekyskolf was caught asleep.

events.title: Raiders at Vimadell
events.text: Raiders strike Vimadell twice in a year; the survivors take refuge in Seevel.

events.title: Collapse at the Gragcha mines
events.text: The deep workings at Gragcha come down on the night shift.
events.backstory: The pit props at Gragcha had not been replaced in years, and in 264 the roof gave way without warning.

events.title: Liareglade is abandoned
events.text: No one at Liareglade can dig deeper, so the hamlet is left to the crows.

events.title: Miners lost at Slelyeld
events.text: The roof comes down in the Slelyeld workings, and the shift below is lost.
events.backstory: Water pooled in the old workings at Slelyeld for a season, and in 269 it burst through into the working face.

events.title: Skeihivik is abandoned
events.text: The lord clears Skeihivik for sheep, and its tenants are turned out onto the road.

events.title: The Peace of Fethyode
events.text: Ykar has the better of it, and Sweyemlel gives up Fethyode and Chryrogorn.

events.title: The new border at Chryrogorn
events.text: By the terms of the peace, Chryrogorn owes its tithes to Ykar from the next harvest.
events.backstory: Chryrogorn was one of the spoils of the War of Fethyode, and changed hands in 270 without a single arrow.

events.title: Ykar takes Fethyode
events.text: Surveyors from Ykar drive new stakes at Fethyode, and Sweyemlel does not send anyone to pull them up.
events.backstory: Fethyode was one of the spoils of the War of Fethyode, and changed hands in 270 without a single arrow.

events.title: High water at Choglosryl
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Rogalat and Choglosryl.
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Choglosryl in 270.

events.title: Grumor is abandoned
events.text: The river takes the well, the fields and the footbridge of Grumor, and the hunters' lodge is let go.
events.backstory: The flood of 270 left Grumor a swamp, and the hunters' lodge was abandoned in 271.

events.title: Sheep replace the folk of Alebrook
events.text: Sheep are worth more to the lord than tenants, and the village at Alebrook is cleared.

events.title: The Roschoch flood
events.text: The river lifts over its banks, and Roschoch stand in brown water.
events.name: The Meglibrook Rising of 276
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Roschoch in 276.

events.title: The fall of the Chargastil galleries
events.text: The roof comes down in the Chargastil workings, and the shift below is lost.
events.backstory: The mine owners at Chargastil skimped on props, and the miners paid for it in 276.

events.title: The Wehol flood
events.text: Water runs through the streets of Wehol and down into the cellars.
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Wehol in 277.

events.title: The Lemethysfe flood
events.text: Water runs through the streets of Lemethysfe and Wetydeth and down into the cellars.
events.backstory: Heavy rain upstream pushed the Meglibrook over its banks in 279, and Lemethysfe was caught asleep.

events.title: High water at Feelyveemse
events.text: The river lifts over its banks, and Feelyveemse stand in brown water.
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Feelyveemse in 279.

events.title: The great flood at Legesde
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Legesde.
events.name: The Drowning of Legesde
events.backstory: Late snows and a sudden thaw sent the Meglibrook through Legesde in 281.

events.title: Collapse at the Legeseld mines
events.text: The roof comes down in the Legeseld workings, and the shift below is lost.
events.backstory: A spring broke into the deep gallery at Legeseld in 284, and the pumps could not keep pace.

events.title: Veihavn is abandoned
events.text: Raiders strike Veihavn twice in a year; the survivors take refuge in Vechrofgorn.

events.title: Koaton is abandoned
events.text: Koaton is attacked in the dark twice in a year, and the mill hamlet is then left to the owls.

events.title: Raiders at Feglen
events.text: Feglen is attacked in the dark twice in a year, and the walled village is then left to the owls.

events.title: Todestead is abandoned
events.text: Sheep are worth more to the lord than tenants, and the farmstead at Todestead is cleared.

events.title: Raiders at Feglade
events.text: Feglade is attacked in the dark twice in a year, and the market village is then left to the owls.

events.title: High water at Sefeethfe
events.text: In the night the river changes its bed, taking mills, byres and cellars at Sefeethfe, Elefeth and Fome.
events.backstory: Wind and a spring tide held back the Geaflow in 288, and the water had to go somewhere.

events.title: House Nydell elected in Sweyemlel
events.text: Delegates gather at Sweyemoth and, after three days of argument, choose House Nydell to rule Sweyemlel.
events.name: The Raising of House Nydell
events.backstory: In 289 a vote at Sweyemoth ended the rule of Riabrook, and House Nydell has held Sweyemlel since.

events.title: Hierarch Gliril of Sweyemlel
events.text: Gliril takes the seat of Sweyemlel.
